3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Lucian was seated across from me at the table, going through documents. Ciara entered the room.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: We were still in Leiren, staying at a modest guesthouse for state employees. Ciara set up a meeting with me and Lucian to go over her plans for education reform after our school visit.

5.speaker: Ciara Walda
5.text: “After the visit yesterday, I couldn't even sleep thinking about that little boy and girl.”

6.speaker: Ciara Walda
6.text: “I have never been more sure of my intentions to reform our education system.”

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Lucian took off his reading glasses and put it on the table.

8.speaker: Player
8.text: “I agree. An educational reform is necessary.”

9.speaker: Player
9.text: “I don't see what's wrong with our education system.”

11.speaker: Ciara Walda
11.text: “Can't you look at it objectively and see what's wrong with it? You can't be serious.”

13.speaker: Ciara Walda
13.text: "Would you say that to a man, Lucian?”

14.speaker: Ciara Walda
14.text: “Those students have to repeat that same Sollist propaganda every single day. They are being brainwashed at an age when their minds need to be free.”

16.speaker: Ciara Walda
16.text: “Those students have to repeat that same Sollist propaganda every single day. They are being brainwashed at an age when their minds need to be free.”

17.speaker: Ciara Walda
17.text: “On top of that, young girls are denied the same opportunity as boys. They're forced into the role of housewife before they even reach puberty!"

18.speaker: Ciara Walda
18.text: “On top of that, young girls are denied the same opportunity as boys. They're forced into the role of housewife before they even reach puberty! Nothing's changed since I went to school."

19.speaker: Ciara Walda
19.text: “Mr. President. We need to bring change. We need to free the minds of these young people. They are our future.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “Very well. What do we need to do for an education reform?”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “Everything is fine as it is. Why change it?”

22.speaker: Ciara Walda
22.text: “I don't think my words are getting through to you.”

23.speaker: Ciara Walda
23.text: “Are you really fine with filling the heads of our children with Sollist propaganda? With teaching girls like Deana that their only value to this country is as vessels for childbearing?"

24.speaker: Ciara Walda
24.text: “You know the words of Artor S. Wisci. You know them better than I do.”

25.speaker: Ciara Walda
25.text: “Education is the premise of progress, in all societies, in all families.”

26.speaker: Ciara Walda
26.text: “We need to reform our education system. Otherwise, Sordland's future is bleak.”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “We have more important matters to think about than education for a bunch of kids.”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “We will not stray away from Soll's path.”

32.speaker: Ciara Walda
32.text: “I can't believe it. This will be seen as a huge mistake when people look back.”

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “You have a point. Alright. So what's your plan?”

36.speaker: Ciara Walda
36.text: “This is actively poisoning young bright minds. Instead of thinking for themselves, they're learning to take things at face value.”

37.speaker: Ciara Walda
37.text: “We also need to ensure boys and girls receive the same instruction. Handcrafts like knitting and sewing should be taught to both sexes, or not at all."

38.speaker: Ciara Walda
38.text: “We need to keep politics out of the curriculum. Soll should only be viewed as a historical figure. Children shouldn't have to repeat his name everyday.”

39.speaker: Ciara Walda
39.text: “Sordland's youth must be technically skilled and capable for the next decade. That won't be possible with the amount of nationalistic indoctrination and narrow-minded thinking found in schools today.”

40.speaker: Ciara Walda
40.text: “Either we raise a generation ready for the challenges of the future or not. What will it be, Mr. President?”

41.speaker: Lucian Galade
41.text: “As much as I respect Colonel Soll, his time has passed. Now is our time. I do think this might be the first step of a larger plan.”

45.speaker: Ciara Walda
45.text: “You will not regret it. I will get to work immediately.”

46.speaker: Ciara Walda
46.text: “I am utterly disappointed. Especially after yesterday's school visit. I thought it would awaken something in you.”

50.speaker: Ciara Walda
50.text: “It will be an uphill battle, considering that the education budget was lowered against my recommendations. But I will give it my best.”

55.speaker: Lucian Galade
55.text: “Now that the decision was made, let's move on.”

56.speaker: Ciara Walda
56.text: “After the budget increase, the ministry quickly began formulating plans on how to effectively use the money.”

63.speaker: Ciara Walda
63.text: “With no change in budget, the ministry was left to its own devices. We made some tough choices but still lack additional funds.”

68.speaker: Ciara Walda
68.text: “But before moving forward, the question of keeping education fully state-funded or allowing for new private schools remains open.”

69.speaker: Player
69.text: “Education should remain as a state service only. Certainly this is the most ideal situation.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “There is a possibility of privatization having negative side effects.”

74.speaker: Ciara Walda
74.text: “Trust me, I know that. It could increase the cost of a quality education, but that is hardly avoidable now anyway.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “Tell us about the benefits of allowing private schools.”

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: Ciara skimmed over her documents before continuing.

77.speaker: Ciara Walda
77.text: “This has led us to think about allowing privatization to at least keep vital education services unaffected.”

78.speaker: Ciara Walda
78.text: “Therefore we are investigating if privatizing education would draw enough funds to conduct investments.”

79.speaker: Ciara Walda
79.text: “It would be a lie to say that a decrease in the budget didn't force us to consider this. We just need the funds even though we don't like privatization.”

80.speaker: Ciara Walda
80.text: “We can manage without additional funds. The only reason I wanted to consider it is to have more money to improve education.”

81.speaker: Ciara Walda
81.text: “We have enough money to improve education in Sordland. We do not need to complicate things further with a privatization incentive.”

82.speaker: Ciara Walda
82.text: “I've made my opinion clear: I'm against it. But it would give us additional funds for education while increasing competition.”

83.speaker: Ciara Walda
83.text: “I agree. The government should be responsible of managing education completely.”

84.speaker: Lucian Galade
84.text: “State education is contrary to our overall economic strategy of promoting a market economy.”

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: A few minutes of deliberation passed.

92.speaker: Ciara Walda
92.text: “There aren't many. But it would give us sorely needed funds and increase competition among schools.”

94.speaker: Lucian Galade
94.text: “Private education is inconsistent with our overall economic strategy of a planned economy.”

95.speaker: Lucian Galade
95.text: “It would go against our overall economic strategy of a planned economy.”

96.speaker: Ciara Walda
96.text: “The reduction of the education budget left our hands completely tied. We are in a budget crisis management situation.”

97.speaker: Lucian Galade
97.text: “It would support our overall economic strategy of promoting a market economy.”

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: She let out a deep sigh.

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “Initiate privatization to draw more funds. This should allow for more competition and quality.” [+2 Government Budget]

103.speaker: Lucian Galade
103.text: “This has been a very productive day. I will be returning to Holsord.”

108.speaker: Ciara Walda
108.text: “Will do. That should be it for now. I will get to work and report back later.”

113.speaker: Player
113.text: “Keep education solely a matter of the state. We need to prevent interference from private interests."

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: We dispersed after spending nearly the entire day together. I took a moment simply to breathe the fresh evening air of Leiren.

117.speaker: Ciara Walda
117.text: “Great. That should be it for now. I will get to work and report back later.”

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: I felt calmer here, somehow. But I would have to return to the chaos of Holsord soon enough.

208.speaker: Narrator
208.text: Ciara looked furious. She shook her head slowly.

209.speaker: Ciara Walda
209.text: “The only way people like me, Nia, Lileas, Gloria, even your wife were able to escape that is because our families were fortunate and well-connected enough to be able to educate us outside of the public school system. Is that the kind of country you want your daughter to grow up in?"

210.speaker: Ciara Walda
210.text: “Women like me, Lileas, Nia, even your wife -- we had to study twice as hard to receive the same university education that you and Lucian took for granted. Is that the kind of country you want your daughter to grow up in?"
